games.title: Shenmue
games.note: Its manual called the timed button prompts 'quick timer events'; the shorter name, QTE, stuck.

games.title: Fahrenheit (Indigo Prophecy)
games.note: Released as Indigo Prophecy in North America, with its sex scenes cut from that version.

games.title: Heavy Rain
games.note: Any of its four playable characters can die, and the story carries on without them.

games.title: Beyond: Two Souls
games.note: Elliot Page and Willem Dafoe starred through full performance capture.

games.title: Detroit: Become Human
games.note: Shows a flowchart after each chapter so you can see the branches you missed.

games.title: Sam & Max Save the World
games.note: Released as six monthly episodes, one of the first successful episodic games.

games.title: Tales of Monkey Island
games.note: Five episodes made with LucasArts, with Monkey Island co-writer Dave Grossman as design director.

games.title: The Walking Dead
games.note: Timed choices came with on-screen notes such as 'Clementine will remember that.'

games.title: The Wolf Among Us
games.note: A noir prequel to Bill Willingham's Fables comics, starring Sheriff Bigby Wolf.

games.title: Life Is Strange
games.note: A photography student discovers she can rewind time; released in five episodes during 2015.

games.title: Remember Me
games.note: Set in a Paris of 2084 where memories can be bought, stolen and rewritten.

games.title: Oxenfree
games.note: Founded by cousins Sean Krankel and Adam Hines; you can cut into conversations at any time while walking.

games.title: Dear Esther
games.note: Began as a free Half-Life 2 mod from a university research project; a remade version sold on Steam in 2012.

games.title: Everybody's Gone to the Rapture
games.note: An English village whose people have vanished, told through glowing echoes of their last days.

games.title: Gone Home
games.note: You explore your family's empty house in 1995 Oregon and piece together your sister's story.

games.title: Tacoma
games.note: A space station's missing crew replayed as AR recordings you can scrub back and forth.

games.title: Firewatch
games.note: Development began with a painting by co-founder Olly Moss in the style of old National Park posters.

games.title: The Unfinished Swan
games.note: Begins on an all-white screen that you reveal by throwing black paint.

games.title: What Remains of Edith Finch
games.note: Each Finch family death is a short game of its own, from a cannery daydream to a comic book.

games.title: Kentucky Route Zero
games.note: Released in five acts between 2013 and 2020.

games.title: Her Story
games.note: You search a 1994 police database by keyword to find clips from seven interviews.

games.title: Telling Lies
games.note: Barlow's spiritual sequel to Her Story, built from secretly recorded video calls.

games.title: Silent Hill: Shattered Memories
games.note: A reimagining of the first Silent Hill with no combat; a therapist's questions change the game around you.

games.title: Aisle
games.note: An interactive-fiction game where you get exactly one command, standing in a supermarket aisle.

games.title: Papers, Please
games.note: Lucas Pope, an American living in Japan, based it on going through border checks while travelling in Asia.

games.title: The Republia Times
games.note: A 48-hour game jam entry where you edit a propaganda newspaper for a dystopian regime.

games.title: Return of the Obra Dinn
games.note: Drawn in 1-bit graphics like early Macintosh games; you deduce the fates of all 60 people aboard.

games.title: The Case of the Golden Idol
games.note: Made by Latvian brothers Andrejs and Ernests Kļaviņš; you fill in blanks with words found at each scene.

games.title: Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney
games.note: First released in Japan on Game Boy Advance; the West got it on Nintendo DS in 2005.

games.title: Ghost Trick: Phantom Detective
games.note: You play a ghost who possesses objects to change the four minutes before each death.

games.title: Professor Layton vs. Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney
games.note: A crossover set in a medieval storybook town where witch trials replace the courtroom.

games.title: The Portopia Serial Murder Case
games.note: First released on NEC's PC-6001; Horii and Koichi Nakamura, who programmed the Famicom port, went on to make Dragon Quest.

games.title: Snatcher
games.note: Kojima's cyberpunk detective story in the spirit of Blade Runner, first released on the PC-8801 and MSX2.

games.title: Policenauts
games.note: A space-colony detective story first released on NEC's PC-9821; it never got an official English release.

games.title: Famicom Detective Club: The Missing Heir
games.note: A Famicom Disk System mystery written by Metroid director Yoshio Sakamoto; remade for Switch in 2021.

games.title: Professor Layton and the Curious Village
games.note: Puzzle-book author Akira Tago led its puzzle team and wrote 30 new puzzles for it.

games.title: Atama no Taisō (puzzle books)
games.note: A best-selling Japanese series of brain-teaser books by Chiba University psychologist Akira Tago.

games.title: Brain Age
games.note: Built around neuroscientist Ryuta Kawashima's brain-training exercises, played with the DS held like a book.

games.title: Danganronpa: Trigger Happy Havoc
games.note: Students trapped in a school by a robot bear must murder or expose each other in class trials.

games.title: Doki Doki Literature Club!
games.note: A free visual novel that poses as a cute dating sim before turning into psychological horror.

games.title: Yume Nikki
games.note: A free RPG Maker game about exploring a girl's dreams, with no dialogue and no combat.

games.title: Eversion
games.note: Looks like a cute Mario-style platformer until each 'eversion' makes the world darker.

games.title: 80 Days
games.note: Meg Jayanth wrote its steampunk trip around the world, with over half a million words of branching text.

games.title: Sorcery!
games.note: An official adaptation of Steve Jackson's 1983 gamebooks, written in inkle's own ink scripting language.

games.title: Sorcery! (gamebooks)
games.note: A four-book Fighting Fantasy spin-off where you cast spells from a book of three-letter codes.

games.title: The Stanley Parable
games.note: Began as a free Half-Life 2 mod in 2011; the expanded standalone version followed in 2013.

games.title: The Beginner's Guide
games.note: Wreden narrates a tour through the unfinished games of a friend he calls Coda.

games.title: Journey
games.note: Strangers can meet and travel together online, but they can only communicate by chiming.

games.title: Flower
games.note: You play the wind, carrying a stream of petals through fields and into a grey city.

games.title: flOw
games.note: Began as Jenova Chen's Flash thesis project at USC, about matching difficulty to the player.

games.title: Abzû
games.note: A wordless dive through ocean ecosystems, directed by Journey's art director Matt Nava.

games.title: Sky: Children of the Light
games.note: A free social adventure where players fly together and share candles; it launched first on iPhone and iPad.

games.title: Night in the Woods
games.note: Funded on Kickstarter in 2013; college dropout Mae returns to her fading Rust Belt hometown.

games.title: Unpacking
games.note: Tells a woman's life story without words, through the belongings she unpacks after each move.

links.extra: Shenmue's director Yu Suzuki is credited with coining the term quick time event.

links.took: Shenmue popularized quick time events, button prompts that play out action scenes.
links.added: Built nearly every action scene from them, alongside dialogue choices and split-screen views.

links.took: Shenmue popularized quick time events for cinematic action.
links.added: Context-sensitive prompts for everyday actions too, from shaving to fistfights.
